summary: Brick tower on a Lake Michigan island near Baileys Harbor, first lit in 1870; steel-clad around 1902, automated by 1944, now a Door County park with a climbable tower.

structures.note: Cream-colored brick, enclosed in a steel shell in 1901 (NRHP) or 1902 (LighthouseFriends, USLHS).

access.note: County park; grounds open half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset; lighthouse and tower May to October, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., tower climb by fee.

facts.agency: Door County (county park), managed with the Door County Maritime Museum

events.note: Johnson reserves the island; Congress approves abandoning Baileys Harbor light and building Cana Island (LighthouseFriends).
Tower and dwelling built; tower of cream-colored Milwaukee brick.
First exhibited 24 January 1870 (LighthouseFriends); county gives 28 January.
Storm of 16 October 1880, called the Alpena Gale by LighthouseFriends.
Renovation under Commander C. E. Clark: fill, 400-foot breakwater, stone oil house, causeway footbridge.
Tower encased in steel plates (USLHS and LighthouseFriends give 1902; the NRHP says 1901).
Frank O'Connor fire near Baileys Harbor: Milwaukee Leader says late Thursday, 2 October; LighthouseFriends says 3 October.
Station receives the Lighthouse Efficiency Flag (Bulletin index; LighthouseFriends dates the award to 1919).
Acetylene light installed mid-November; station closed in winter.
Ross F. Wright, last civilian keeper.
Electric power lines strung across the causeway (LighthouseFriends).
Coast Guard leases the dwelling to a private family as a summer residence for about 25 years.
Control given to the Door County Maritime Museum (LighthouseFriends); museum works with the Coast Guard from 1970 (county).
Bureau of Land Management transfers the land to Door County for a park, 27 April 2006 (county); LighthouseFriends dates the transfer to 2007.

wrecks.outcome: Fire near Baileys Harbor, late Thursday, per the Milwaukee Leader of 3 October 1919, which says a crew of 21 was rescued by the Baileys Harbor coast guard crew. LighthouseFriends dates the fire to 4 p.m. on 3 October and says the keepers towed the crew ashore (its caption says the Coast Guard took them onto Baileys Harbor). The fiscal 1920 Commissioner record lists the Cana Island keeper as rescuing the crew from the burned vessel. The county says it burned to the waterline in 1919.

corrections.why: USLHS gives the light as 89 ft (27.1 m) above mean high water and the museum calls the tower 89 feet tall. The record's 24.0 m matches neither.
Land transferred to Door County in 2006 to be used as a park; the county and the museum manage the island and lighthouse.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends gives 24 January 1870 and the county page 28 January for the first official lighting. Both agree the light was first lit in 1870.
The record's 24.0 m tower height does not match USLHS (89 ft, 27.1 m above mean high water) or the museum's 89-foot tower. The NRHP also gives about 27 m above the ground.

notes_for_editor: CHECKED 2026-10-22 against the sources and the cached pages. Quotes: all 124 found on the first run. UNRESOLVED: (1) Frank O'Connor date and rescue: Milwaukee Leader, 3 Oct 1919 p.9 (checked, OCR and text): fire 'late Thursday' (2 Oct), crew of 21 rescued by the Baileys Harbor coast guard crew. LighthouseFriends: fire at 4 p.m. on 3 Oct; keepers Knudsen and assistant towed lifeboats ashore; caption says Coast Guard took crew onto Baileys Harbour. Commissioner fiscal 1920 list (page image read, p.60): O. H. Knudsen, keeper, Cana Island, 'Rescued crew from burned vessel', aided vessel Frank O'Connor. The story gives all three. (2) Steel casing: NRHP 1901 vs LighthouseFriends June-Aug 1902 vs USLHS 1902. (3) Causeway: NRHP gravel causeway ca. 1917 vs LighthouseFriends natural causeway. (4) Automation and power: county 1944; LighthouseFriends electricity 1934; roster has Drezdzon head keeper to 1946. (5) Ownership: county BLM transfer 27 Apr 2006; LighthouseFriends 2007. (6) Janda caretaker years: county 1976-1995; LighthouseFriends from 1977. (7) First lit: 24 Jan (LighthouseFriends) vs 28 Jan (county, first official lighting). IMAGE CHECKS: the 1916 (scan p.170, printed p.61) and 1920 (scan p.558, printed p.60) pages were read as images. Both are titled 'Saving of Life and Property by Vessels or Employees of the Lighthouse Service', i.e. rescue tables, not personnel lists; the footnotes were relabelled. The 1916 line reads 'C. A. Stram, keeper; M. Weiss, assistant keeper, Cana Island Light Station, Wis.' (OCR had 'Strain'); the rescue entry is 'Motor boat Martha S., Oconto' with 'Pulled boat, which had run on rocks, out of danger'. The 1920 line reads 'O. H. Knudsen, keeper, Cana Island Light Station, Wis.' (OCR had 'O. 1J.'). FISCAL YEARS: the 1901 boathouse repair is given as fiscal 1901 (year ended 30 June 1901); the 1896-97 report is named as the fiscal years 1896 and 1897. YEAR OMITTED: the 2025 storm year was removed from the story and the 2025 event from events, because no fetchable page states the year. The museum page gives 'Saturday, August 9' and 'Wednesday, August 13' with no year; MLive's URL is dated 2025/08 but the page returned HTTP 403. 1933 BULLETIN: the 'Lights seen at unusual distances' note gives no year, so 1932 was removed. Private residents: the family who leased the dwelling 1945-70 is not named. The Jandas are named only as caretakers, as the county page names them. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: its facts are paraphrased, and its Sanderson report (1880) is second-hand. The 1880 Board report is not in the corpus. The 1902 Board report is not in the corpus, so the steel-casing year is not settled here. Wikipedia consulted as a lead only; not cited.
